# TemporalDetail with real vectors: tables (generated by tools/eval/td_vectors/summarize.py)

## 1. Frame types: quality and fine-band detail vs master (full 1080p frames, frames 2..69)

fine band H = x - Gaussian(sigma 1 px). `keep` = E[H(C)^2]/E[H(M)^2] (detail energy kept, can exceed 1 with coding noise); `hb err` = E[H(M-C)^2] (10-bit codes^2); `grain/incoh` = temporally incoherent master fine band (grain, noise, new content); `struct err` = E[H(S-C)^2] against the master's 5-frame motion-compensated structure S.

## 2. Recoverable from the decoded I/P references after motion compensation (per-block ORACLE ceilings)

References: previous + next anchor (I/P), plus the nearest I frame within 12 frames for B. Per 16 px block the best reference and strength a in [0,1] are chosen WITH the master, so these are upper bounds. dB = PSNR gain on that frame type. `% gap` = hb gain / (PSNR(I+P) - PSNR(B)). `warp` = mean PSNR (10-bit peak) of a warped decoded reference against the master frame (alignment quality). Sources: `X:coded` = vectors from the decoded frames (engine), `X:master` = vectors from the uncompressed master applied to the decoded frames (near-ideal).

## 3. TemporalDetail CPU model, designed gates (default), full 1080p, 72 frames
